findings.text: FOLLOW-ON. A walrus whose target sits in a def's or a lambda's DEFAULT expression binds in the scope CONTAINING the def, so the module-level `_resolve = lambda index=(_LABEL_RE := 0): index` and the module-level `def build(x=(_FIFTH_DEF := 7)): return x` both leave their name in the module namespace (runpy on each shape: the module namespace contains _LABEL_RE / _FIFTH_DEF), while the delivered walk reports no declaration for either, because it treats every FunctionDef, AsyncFunctionDef and Lambda on the path as disqualifying without asking which part of the def the expression sits in. Demonstrated through the guard itself: with the lambda-default rival appended to imas_ambix/agent/bench.py the whole three-file guard file is 12 passed (replay-c5-lambda-default-walrus-rival.txt) while runpy on that same mutated bench.py exports _LABEL_RE (an int, present in the namespace), against a control that does redden on the same name bound the other way -- a module-level comprehension walrus in bench.py gives 1 failed, 11 passed, naming bench.py as a second owner (replay-c3-controlE-walrus-rival.txt). The module docstring's list of deliberately-uncovered shapes (augmented assignment, except-as, for/with targets, parameter names, globals()[...] subscript) does not name defaults; a reader takes the walrus rule to cover every expression whose binding escapes its own comprehension, and a default expression escapes its def. Reachability is low -- no reader of this package second-sources the exposition grammar in a lambda default -- so this is a boundary the docstring should state (or the walk should carry, by stepping over a def whose path never enters the def's body) rather than a defect in the two directions this round repaired; both of those are confirmed below. Related nuance found while probing, recorded rather than charged: `class Grammar: pairs = [(_X := i) for i in range(3)]` is counted by the scan, but such a module cannot be imported at all (compile raises SyntaxError while ast.parse accepts it), so the counted declaration can never be reachable.

item_verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit. b596e011 is the repair and touches tests/test_agent_bench_shared_reader.py only (185 insertions, 42 deletions): the walk becomes a module-root walk carrying the walrus flag, _declares passes assignment_expression for NamedExpr only. 9f960324 records it. bench.py is untouched by both: its blob is 9e6186e3b8de587239229fa86659f06bd431370c at HEAD and at b596e011's parent, re-derived here. The two new rule halves each carry a counterpart test and a library comment describing the mechanism it counts, not the round it came from. No plan label, ticket reference, version suffix or author attribution appears in any added name, comment or docstring; regex scans over the added lines returned one hit, the English word steps in the docstring sentence the walk steps over comprehensions, which is prose about the walk, not a stage identifier. No hunk lands outside the declared write paths.
item_verdicts.done_when: The done-when is the two repaired directions each shown load-bearing, and every mutation the node records was replayed here on ITS OWN scratch trees built from the delivered bytes rather than read. The guard file's sha256 at the revision I read (9f960324) is aed6138b1e9e8deb4a941ccdc6e463d42f2e8fe082096cabe976f59b09f3d6a1, byte-identical to the gated-content digest the node recorded. Nine cases, each with the mutation asserted-present before running and the mutated file digests logged: baseline 12 passed; the function-local class rival 12 passed (the node's control D, green as recorded); the same rival under the pre-repair walk 2 failed, 10 passed, the failures being the whole-package owner test and the class-body test (control D' as recorded); the module-level walrus rival 1 failed, 11 passed on the whole-package owner test (control E as recorded); the same rival with the walrus flag dropped 1 failed, 11 passed on the dedicated walrus test (control E' as recorded); the guarded tuple narrowed from five entries to four 1 failed, 11 passed on the guarded-set assertion alone -- the tuple is asserted, not assumed; `return False` as the first statement of the walk 3 failed, 9 passed, including the innocent-module test (the round-1 control A direction, whose log names the older function name _is_function_local -- that name is gone from the delivered file, so the equivalent first-statement mutation was applied to _is_local and the adaptation is stated rather than hidden); the parse call wrapped in try/except SyntaxError/continue 1 failed, 11 passed with DID NOT RAISE SyntaxError on the parse-error test alone (control C as recorded). Every recorded outcome reproduces. The one case the node does not carry is the fifth case above: the lambda-default rival leaves the guard green at 12 passed while the module really exports the name.
item_verdicts.goal: The round's stated goal is that the walk reach the module root and that the walrus asymmetry be handled in both directions. Both were re-derived with real modules rather than read. Four shapes, each a module in a scratch package, classified by the DELIVERED scan functions and independently by runpy on the same module: a class body inside a function is NOT counted (scan reports {}, runpy's module namespace holds only the function name); a class body at module level IS counted (the class object is a module attribute, so a caller can resolve through it); a module-level comprehension walrus IS counted (runpy shows the name in the module namespace); a comprehension's own loop target is NOT counted (runpy shows the name absent). All four answers are correct. A plain module-level assignment is counted, which is the check that the classifier sees something known present before its negative results are trusted. The fifth-shape hunt found one shape the walk still gets wrong, carried as the finding: a walrus in a def's or lambda's DEFAULT binds in the containing scope and is reported as local. Two further shapes answer correctly (a walrus in a nested module-level comprehension is counted and runpy confirms it exports; a walrus inside a comprehension inside a function is not counted and runpy confirms it does not escape). A definition under if TYPE_CHECKING is counted, which is the intended direction for a textual second declaration -- the runtime namespace shows nothing there because the guard is false, so that shape is an intended exception to the runtime-namespace criterion, not a disagreement with it. Docked for the default-expression gap.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read in full and re-derived wherever checkable. The bench.py blob it quotes is confirmed at both revisions. The gated-content sha256 it quotes is the sha256 of the guard file at the revision I read. Every control outcome it reports reproduces on the delivered bytes, including the failing test names. Its three disclosed process matters stand: the round-1 login-node run is named as not the gate and the all_debug runs behind it are the ones offered; the strawman first attempt of control B and the killed hung driver are disclosed with the pids rather than hidden; the read-live-log misreading and the killed backgrounded driver are disclosed and their superseded logs retained. Its own round-2 replay of the round-1 controls on a scratch tree differing by one trailing newline was noted by the previous review as a nit; the replays recorded here ran on the exact delivered bytes, which closes it. Docked lightly because the default-expression boundary is not stated anywhere in the delivery.
item_verdicts.write_paths: Declared four paths for the node (bench.py, the guard test file, the evidence archive, the plan). The repair commit touches the guard test file alone; the recording commit touches the evidence archive and the plan; bench.py carries no diff in either, re-derived as above. The production call sites of the guarded reader were checked and named: imas_ambix/agent/serving_receipts.py:75 (engine_metrics.read_metrics), imas_ambix/agent/lane.py:403 and :408 (parse_metrics, detect_family) with :314, :317 and :337-342 (eligible_samples, series_first, series_labels and the KV-pool label), and imas_ambix/agent/bench.py:1008 (read_metrics(text).spec_decode inside _spec_decode_snapshot). The guard itself is a test module and has NO production call site; what this review verifies is that those three production modules resolve the exposition grammar through the one declaring module, and that the assertion is not vacuous -- appending a second owner reddens it (replay-c3), which is the contrast the fifth-case blindness needs. The plan's state scalars are outside every hunk.

justifications.durability: The heavy gate ran on all_debug allocations and the evidence record carries the full accounting with the machine per run; the journal keeps controls, logs, digests and the ledger of disclosures, and the superseded logs are retained rather than deleted. The node's self-disclosure of a round-1 login-node run and of two killed background drivers is exactly the accounting that makes a record checkable. Docked three for the round-1 login-node run itself, which the node correctly names as not the gate but which happened, and for leaving the default-expression boundary unstated.
justifications.evidence: Strong. The gated content's digest matches the bytes at the revision read; the bench.py blob identity is confirmed at both revisions; every control outcome reproduces on those exact bytes with the same failing test names; the guarded tuple is asserted and narrowing it reddens; the sixth round's scratch-tree trailing-newline caveat from the previous review is closed by replays on the delivered bytes. Docked two because the fifth case shows a rival the guard cannot see while the evidence record presents the walrus rule as complete.
justifications.fit: The rule serves the plan's purpose: one owner for the exposition grammar, with the guard refusing to be switched off by innocent modules. Every repair narrows the rule toward what a caller can actually resolve through, which is the plan's own criterion. Docked two for the same boundary gap.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Both named directions are implemented as described and each is correct on real modules, re-derived by this review rather than read: the module-root walk spares a class body inside a function and still counts a module-level class body, and the walrus flag counts a module-level comprehension target while leaving a comprehension's own loop target alone. The third finding's repair (literal expectations) is present and the literals equal the fixture's own counters. Docked three because the walk's own principle -- a walrus binds in the scope containing the expression that holds it -- is violated at one more position, a def or lambda DEFAULT, which the delivery neither handles nor names as out of scope.
justifications.scope_discipline: Perfect as measured. Only the declared paths carry hunks; bench.py is byte-identical to its base revision at both revisions checked; no plan or sprint state is mutated by the commits under review; the naming scan over the added lines returned a single hit that is the English word steps in docstring prose, with no plan label, ticket reference, version suffix or attribution anywhere in the added lines.

raw_text: CONFIRMING REVIEW, round three, of r-20260921T085923815245-one-owner-guard-widens-to-any-indentation, read in place at 9f960324 (worktree HEAD), covering the repair commit b596e011. Verdict: the two directions the round set out to repair are repaired and each is shown load-bearing by a counterpart run; the four named shapes answer correctly on real modules; the guard remains blind to one further shape, a walrus in a def or lambda default, recorded as a FOLLOW-ON. The deliverable, tests/test_agent_bench_shared_reader.py, is the sole code artifact. Nothing in this review changes the code: the write scope is this record and this review's own journal.
